claims.text: Sequence-level probability estimates in large language models do not reliably rank-order open-ended generations by quality.
Reformulating open-ended generation into token-level prediction tasks allows leveraging token-level calibration to improve confidence scoring.
Self-evaluation based hybrid scoring with a NONE OF THE ABOVE option achieves 75.34% Calibration-AUC on TruthfulQA using PaLM-2 Large.
Self-evaluation based hybrid scoring with a NONE OF THE ABOVE option achieves 58.10% Selective-AUC on TruthfulQA using PaLM-2 Large.

evidence.description: Studies show that language models' sequence probabilities on open-ended generations do not reliably rank-order outputs by quality, yielding Calibration-AUC below 50% on TruthfulQA.
The authors propose reducing free-form generation scoring to multiple-choice and true/false evaluation tasks using prompt formats that extract token-level logits or probabilities.
Table 1 reports a Calibration-AUC of 75.34% for 'Hybrid w/ nota' on TruthfulQA with PaLM-2 Large, compared to 39.80% for sequence likelihood.
Table 1 reports a Selective-AUC of 58.10% for 'Hybrid w/ nota' on TruthfulQA with PaLM-2 Large, compared to 33.63% for sequence likelihood.

methodologies.name: Sample and Select and Eval (Hybrid)
methodologies.description: A hybrid zero-shot self-evaluation protocol that selects candidate answers via multi-choice selection prompt and assigns a confidence score using pointwise true/false evaluation penalized by a 'None of the above' option probability.

limitations.text: Sequence-level likelihood is inherently biased toward sequence length, underestimating probabilities for longer sentences.
Self-evaluation increases inference time by 1 to 2 additional forward passes per sample.
API limitations restricting output log-probabilities to only the top 5 candidates prevented full evaluation of multi-choice methods on certain models such as GPT-3.

future_work.text: Improving the quality calibration of sequence-level scores directly during model training and fine-tuning.
